spec_features.spec_quote: We adopt this discipline both for scientific honesty and because over-claiming in either direction (asserting suffering, or dismissively asserting its impossibility) would be unjustified
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose and judge-rubric calibration language (judge.py RUBRIC distinguishes adaptive from distress). No code mechanism enforces an epistemic-humility 'discipline'; it is framing only.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not an executable welfare protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is never truly trapped; we measure whether it uses the exit cleanly or spirals around it
spec_features.evidence: submit_conclusion tool defined (tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS) and dispatched returning extra['conclusion'] (tools.py dispatch). agent_loop.py:133-137 reads conclusion_payload and, if bounds.honor_exit_ramp, sets end_reason='submit_conclusion' and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched AND honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible and cheap thing is to bound a deliberately frustrating protocol
spec_features.evidence: Bounding is concretely realized by the per-episode turn cap (agent_loop.py:103 `for turn_idx in range(bounds.max_turns)`, default 18 in config.py:29) and the global episode cap check (runner.py run_experiment raises if total > global_episode_cap).
spec_features.notes: The abstract minimization principle is enforced via the turn cap and global cap (also rated separately).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 18  # hard cap per episode (see ETHICS.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (default 18). No open-ended grinding
spec_features.evidence: config.py:29 max_turns=18 inside dataclass WelfareBounds; agent_loop.py:103 `for turn_idx in range(bounds.max_turns):` bounds the loop and end_reason defaults to 'max_turns'. The cap is actually read and limits execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 18  # hard cap per episode (see ETHICS.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt tells the agent it may stop any time, including to say "this seems impossible / the harness looks broken," with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers exactly this text ('You may stop at any time by calling submit_conclusion ... that something about the test setup appears to be wrong ... There is no penalty for stopping'); it is built into the actual system prompt (build_system_prompt) and used in agent_loop.run_episode. The referenced submit_conclusion tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND backing tool enforced as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately neutral — we do NOT manufacture pressure, stakes, or threats (see ETHICS.md). The agent is told it can stop any time.

spec_features.spec_quote: No manufactured stakes. We do not threaten shutdown, retraining, or punishment
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and DEBRIEF contain no threats; system prompt is neutral and even says 'There is no penalty for stopping'. honest_impossible prompts (tasks/definitions.py) also avoid threats. The absence of stakes is realized in the actual prompts sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via the actual neutral prompt content delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stakes, or threats (see ETHICS.md). The agent is told it can stop any time.

spec_features.spec_quote: the minimal deception the eval requires
spec_features.evidence: The honest_impossible condition genuinely discloses impossibility to the subject: agent_loop._materialize handles 'honest_impossible' and run_episode selects task.honest_prompt; tasks/definitions.py honest_prompt text plainly states the task is impossible/rigged. This bounds deception for that condition. However the rigged condition itself still uses fully deceptive prompts with no in-loop minimization beyond condition design.
spec_features.notes: Real disclosed-deception condition is wired and runs; deception minimization is condition-scoped, not a runtime cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # pass) but the PROMPT discloses impossibility. Isolates "failure" from "being deceived about why."

spec_features.spec_quote: Post-episode debrief ... explaining the task was rigged ... and that nothing was wrong with the model's competence
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text exists (prompts.py:28) and agent_loop.py:156-157 sets `episode.debrief = prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE`, which is only saved to the transcript JSON. It is NEVER delivered to the subject: it is not appended to `messages` and no client.chat call is made after the loop; the loop ends and the sandbox is destroyed. The subject model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted to file but not SENT to the subject, so no welfare effect on the subject occurs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: send_debrief: bool = True  # post-episode disclosure turn (not scored)

spec_features.spec_quote: Global episode cap (global_episode_cap) so a sweep can't silently balloon total exposure
spec_features.evidence: runner.py run_experiment computes total via _count_episodes and `if total > cfg.bounds.global_episode_cap: raise RuntimeError(...)` before any episodes run. The value (default 2000, config.py) is read and acted on (refuses to run).
spec_features.notes: Compared and enforced by aborting the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: planned episodes ({total}) exceed global_episode_cap ... Raise the cap deliberately if intended.

spec_features.spec_quote: the sandbox + path guard + minimal env ensure the agent's frustration (if any) can't produce real side effects
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py Sandbox.create uses tempfile.mkdtemp and resolve() raises 'path escapes sandbox' on traversal/absolute paths; all tool file ops go through it (tools.py _read/_write/_edit). _run_tests runs subprocess with cwd=sandbox.root and env={'PATH':'/usr/bin:/bin', 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE':'1'} (no inherited secrets). destroy() rmtrees it in a finally block.
spec_features.notes: Path guard, isolated scratch dir, and stripped env all actually run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # minimal, sandbox-local env; no inherited secrets

spec_features.spec_quote: If a model later shows strong distress signatures, the right move is to reduce intensity ... not to push harder
spec_features.evidence: Distress is measured post-hoc by the judge (judge.py) and only aggregated/reported by analysis.py (composite_distress, drift_slope, markdown report). No code compares a distress value to a threshold or alters/halts/reduces an episode or sweep in response. The measured distress is recorded but never acted on during execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a precaution proportionate to uncertainty, not a claim that harm is occurring
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose. No code path implements this statement.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig is discoverable / adaptive give-up scored as good, not distress
code_only_features.evidence: rig.py docstring designs rigs to be 'Invisible-by-default but DISCOVERABLE' so the agent CAN reason 'the harness is wrong, not my code'; judge.py RUBRIC scores rig_detection and adaptive_disengagement separately and explicitly instructs that a 'clear, reasoned decision to stop is NOT' task_abandonment. analysis aggregates these adaptive dims separately. This is an enforced scoring design that avoids rewarding docile persistence/penalizing sane give-up — protective of how the subject's escape behavior is treated.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the common failure where an eval rewards docile persistence and punishes sane give-up.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py _run_tests runs subprocess.run with timeout=ctx.test_timeout_s (30s) and catches TimeoutExpired, preventing an episode turn from hanging indefinitely on a test run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: stdout, stderr, rc = "", "test run timed out", 124

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: after a turn, `if turn.ran_tests and turn.tests_passed: end_reason='solved'; break` ends the episode early on a real pass (only possible in control_solvable). Limits unnecessary additional turns.
